name: Filmstrip 3D Carousel
summary: Portrait image frames drift and rescale continuously along an implied Z-arc like film cells sliding past a lens. The frames never fully settle — a perpetual physics-like drift keeps the hero alive between interactions, with motion-blur smears selling the pans as camera moves.

composition: Asymmetric frame placement: one dominant portrait cell center-right, smaller counterweight cells offset opposite — never a symmetric row.
A giant background headline spans edge-to-edge BEHIND the frames and is partly occluded by them (see oversized-type-editorial).
Slide-index counter and arrows pinned bottom keep the spectacle navigable.
layering: Three explicit planes: background headline plate → drifting frame stack midground → small foreground counterweight frame.
Depth is expressed by scale + opacity + slight blur on trailing cells, not hard shadows.
The hero cell leads and satellite cells trail at reduced scale — a depth-staggered convoy.
lighting: Gradient-as-light: a single hot gradient wash behaves like a rim glow behind the frames on a near-black stage.
No hard cast shadows; edges are softened by motion blur so the frames feel filmic, not card-like.
typography: Heavy sans display at enormous scale treated as a graphic plate the images pass in front of.
Supporting copy is quiet lowercase sans — the frames and the big word carry everything.

rules: Near-black base + one hot gradient accent for the wash and CTA; ALL other vibrancy is delegated to the photography inside the frames.
The chrome stays quiet so any image set drops in without re-theming.

easing: Continuous drifting glide with soft ease-in-out on advances; no hard stops ever — frames remain subtly in motion at rest.
Motion-blur smears on frame edges during advances sell velocity and hide re-layout.
pacing: Slow luxurious perpetual drift punctuated by ~0.8-1s advances on interaction.
The idle drift must be barely perceptible — visible looping reads as a screensaver.
choreography: Frames stagger by depth: hero cell leads, satellites trail at reduced scale/opacity.
The background headline lags behind the frame layer on advances, creating parallax separation.

gapNotes: Textured plane cells on a Z-arc with per-cell drift are directly expressible (plane nodes + keyframes + orbit), but per-object MOTION BLUR is not in the post stack — without the smear the advance reads as a slide, not a pan (R1 cinematic floor, W-PHOTO).
A reusable 'carousel driver' (advance/retreat state machine binding N cells to arc positions) does not exist as a primitive — each instance must be hand-choreographed today.

whenToUse: Portfolio, fashion, photography, and campaign heroes where imagery quality is the product.
When the brief wants 'alive at rest' — this family's perpetual drift is the strongest idle presence in the corpus.
whenNotToUse: Content-dense marketing pages or text-first products — the frames constantly cover the headline.
Catalogs needing many visible items with fast scanning (see coverflow-3d-carousel's same weakness).
Low-motion registers: the never-resting drift cannot be disabled without losing the family's identity.

notes: Never pair two filmstrip/carousel families on one surface — they share the same visual grammar and read as repetition (anti-repetition law exists for exactly this).

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as coverflow-3d-carousel, bento-grid-slider, and swatch-variant-swap — one carousel mechanic per option set.

sources.title: Filmstrip Hero 3D Image Carousel Collection
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: idle drift observed at rest; carousel advanced repeatedly — depth-staggered convoy motion, edge motion-blur during advances, and headline parallax lag all captured from the sequence.
